comment:
Emit seeds/aperture_frame.json -- APERTURE IS A FRAME: chosen, forced, or negotiated.

`observer_aperture` made aperture graph data, but as a single authored list on the
observer -- an acuity it simply HAS. That is incomplete. An aperture is a FRAME
you are viewing in, and a frame has provenance: you can choose it, it can be
forced on you, or you can negotiate it with someone else.

This is the reference-frame sense, not the Fillmore `Frame` (which is language
semantics and is left alone). And it is not a metaphor here: `CLAUDE.md`'s
frame/continuum invariant puts every lossy or real-valued map in
`Hom(frame, frame)` rather than inside a frame's coordinates, and the projection
`observer_aperture` performs IS such a map -- world frame to observer frame, with
the collapse marker naming exactly what the map discards.

Two things follow, and the second is the whole point.

**The effective aperture is a MEET.** Every frame in force narrows what you
resolve, so `resolves` stops being authored and becomes derived: the fold of
`Intersect` over your own maximum acuity and every frame currently on you. An
observer declares its PHYSIOLOGY (`ap_full`); the frames decide the rest.

**The three modes decode identically and differ entirely in RECOURSE.** This is
the testable content -- same residual, three different things you may do about it:

  * CHOSEN -- you narrowed your own attention, so you may widen it unilaterally.
    An outstanding residual is a reason to look harder, and `ap_relax_chosen`
    drops the frame and re-arms the decode. Attention, mechanically.
  * FORCED -- someone or something else narrowed it, and you cannot lift it. An
    outstanding residual here is a gap you can DETECT and cannot close alone, so
    it opens a `SelfConcern` on the existing human-gated spine. This is the
    knowing-THAT-without-knowing-WHAT case from `ONE_LOOP_MANY_GRAINS.md`, one
    level up: not merely unresolved, but unresolvable BY YOU.
  * NEGOTIATED -- it binds several parties, so no one may change it alone. A
    proposal takes effect only when every bound party has accepted; a unilateral
    accept does nothing at all.

An agent that can only be forced has no attention; one that can only choose has
no social constraint; one that cannot negotiate cannot establish common ground.

rules.name: af_effective_aperture
rules.comment: The effective aperture is the MEET of the observer's own maximum acuity and every frame in force on it, whatever the provenance. `resolves` is therefore DERIVED, not authored: an observer declares its physiology (`ap_full`) and the frames decide the rest. Re-arms on any change in how many frames are in force -- which is what makes dropping a chosen frame actually widen perception.

rules.name: af_relax_chosen
rules.comment: CHOSEN recourse. You narrowed your own attention, so an outstanding residual is a reason to widen it -- and you may, unilaterally. Dropping the frame re-arms `af_effective_aperture`, which re-arms the decode. Attention as a graph move rather than a parameter.

rules.name: af_forced_residual_is_a_concern
rules.comment: FORCED recourse -- there is none, and that is the point. The residual is identical to the chosen case; what differs is that the observer cannot lift the frame. So it files what it CAN do: record that something here is unresolved and not resolvable by it alone. Knowing THAT without knowing WHAT, one level up -- and it lands on the existing human-gated spine (promote -> StandingConcern -> experiment), so another party can act on it.

rules.name: af_adopt_when_every_party_accepts
rules.comment: NEGOTIATED recourse. The frame binds several parties, so no one may change it alone: the offered aperture attaches only once every bound party has accepted. A unilateral accept does nothing -- which is the whole difference from `chose_aperture`, and the reason common ground is not the same operation as attention.

rules.name: af_retract_when_every_party_accepts
rules.comment:
RENEGOTIATION -- the only way out of a negotiated frame, and the exact mirror of adoption: it comes off when every bound party accepts that it should, and not before. A frame one party could drop alone would just be a chosen frame with extra steps, which is why `af_relax_chosen` deliberately never touches this edge.

Recorded because it was not designed: this rule was missing until APERTURE_PATHOLOGIES.md asked what the SECOND intervention on a shared blind spot would be. The rule the machinery lacked turned out to be the treatment the mechanism implies. Dropping the edge re-arms `af_effective_aperture` (the frame count changes), which bumps the generation, which invalidates every view taken through the retracted frame -- so perception genuinely widens rather than the edge merely disappearing.

rules.name: af_count_chosen_dwell
rules.comment: P2.C4.4 questioning counter: when a chosen frame is in force and the current generation's percept has been decoded without triggering `af_relax_chosen` (residual magnitude below `ap_relax_tolerance`), increment `obs.ap_chosen_dwell` once for this generation.

rules.name: af_probe_project_held
rules.comment: P2.C4.4 probe codebook projection: once `ap_chosen_dwell >= ap_question_after`, project each held part through `ap_probe_resolves` (bypassing `chose_aperture` while still honouring `forced_aperture` and `agreed_aperture`).

rules.name: af_probe_project_percept
rules.comment: P2.C4.4 probe percept projection & decode: once all held parts are probe-projected for the current generation, project the percept through `ap_probe_resolves` and decode its residual against the probe codebook.

rules.name: af_question_drop_hiding_frame
rules.comment: P2.C4.4 questioning verdict (drop): if the probe view (bypassing chosen frames) reveals a larger residual than the framed view, the chosen frame is hiding an unresolved distinction (`APERTURE_PATHOLOGIES.md` §1). Drop `chose_aperture` unilaterally and file no `SelfConcern`.

rules.name: af_question_keep_honest_frame
rules.comment: P2.C4.4 questioning verdict (keep): if the probe view's residual is no larger than the framed view's residual, the chosen frame is not hiding an unresolved distinction; keep the frame and reset `ap_chosen_dwell`.
